magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is fundamentally theologically neutral: it speaks of the development and comparison of technological tools, without explicit assertions about God, man, or morality that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. Its anticipation of local models and evaluation of a particular tool as best are technological judgments, not religious teaching; the passage does not consider how such technology should be directed toward human dignity and the common good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic approach neither demonizes nor idolizes technology, but judges its use by whether it serves truth, human dignity, and the common good. The human person, created in the image of God (Gen 1:26), must not be subordinated to efficiency or profit, and artificial intelligence should assist human discernment, not replace it.
concerns_en: Technological progress and efficiency are presented as expected goals, without consideration of potential consequences for human labor, privacy, truth, or the common good; this is an omission in a moral context, not a direct contradiction to Catholic teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: Chinese models and the future: Claude Code without internet in a few years
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares Chinese open source models with Opus 5.5 and announces local models
sections.content_en:
The same participant asks where Chinese models are today compared to Anthropic and other major players. He notes that there was a lot of talk about Qwen and similar models, but that earlier they had problems with the English language, for example that they did not understand slang.

Matija Stepanić replies that of the Chinese open source models he has not tried anything except **DeepSeek**. He recalls the moment when, as he says, „in quotation marks” the Chinese used OpenAI's models for about a million and a half dollars, trained their own, and then released DeepSeek as open source and publicly showed how *reasoning* works. In parallel, Alibaba is developing Qwen models. He also installed Kimi on his computer, but he never launched Kimi coding because one would have to pay 15 euros, and what he has works well.

### Player number one

Stepanić's assessment is clear: **Anthropic's Claude Code with Opus 5.5 is player number one**. All the others follow and copy it, and probably develop their own tools precisely with it. The race continues, and as the leading models advance, open source will advance as well. That is why he expects that in a few years it will be possible to use a completely open source solution on one's own computer, that is, Claude Code that works **without internet**. The participant summarizes this as a local LLM, which the guest confirms.

Meanwhile, one participant from the audience recommends an add-on that he calls **Claude Router**. According to his words, when tokens are spent, such an add-on can redirect work to other, free models. He is not sure about the exact name, but advises searching the internet for a list of the five most important add-ons for Claude, among which it should be found.

sections.subtitle: Umjesto planiranih sat vremena, dva sata pitanja i poziv na nove susrete
sections.screenshot_description: Matija Stepanić zahvaljuje publici na kraju predavanja
sections.content:
Na kraju Matija Stepanić priznaje da je predavanje, s pitanjima, trajalo dva sata. Kada ga je Domagoj pozvao, predvidio je trideset minuta izlaganja i trideset minuta pitanja, a odgovor je bio da dvorana ostaje otvorena do 20 sati. Tako je i bilo.

Zahvaljuje publici na pažnji i najavljuje da je ideja ovakve susrete nastaviti. Poručuje da bi rado došao i u ulozi slušatelja te postavljao pitanja kad god netko od prisutnih bude imao vlastiti projekt ili priču za ispričati.

Večer završava pozivom iz dvorane da sudionici ne odu odmah kući, nego da ostanu na kiflicama i sokovima i nastave razgovor u neformalnom ozračju, u duhu zajednice koju inkubator želi graditi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: zahvalnost, razmjena znanja, gostoljubivost i njegovanje zajednice u poslovnom okruženju nisu u sukobu s vjerom. Ipak, riječ je o društvenom završetku predavanja, a ne o izričitom promicanju kršćanskog nauka.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko promišljanje o poslovnom životu potiče da se rad shvaća kao poziv na služenje drugima te da se poslovni odnosi grade kao zajednice osoba, a ne samo kao sredstva vlastitog probitka. U tom svjetlu poziv na daljnji razgovor i susrete može biti vrijedan ako se zajedništvo očituje u poštovanju dostojanstva drugih i težnji za općim dobrom. Odlomak ne navodi konkretne biblijske tvrdnje, pa se ne može utvrditi posebna povezanost s određenim odlomkom Svetoga pisma.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: gratitude, sharing of knowledge, hospitality, and nurturing community in a business environment are not in conflict with faith. Still, it is a social conclusion to a lecture, rather than an explicit promotion of Christian teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic reflection on business life encourages work to be understood as a vocation to serve others and business relationships to be built as communities of persons, not merely as instruments of self-advancement. In this light, the invitation to further conversation and meetings can be valuable if communion is manifested in respecting the dignity of others and striving for the common good. The passage cites no specific biblical assertions, so a particular connection to a specific passage of Sacred Scripture cannot be established.

sections.subtitle_en: Instead of the planned one hour, two hours of questions and an invitation to new gatherings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matija Stepanić thanks the audience at the end of the lecture
sections.content_en:
At the end, Matija Stepanić admits that the lecture, with questions, lasted two hours. When Domagoj invited him, he planned thirty minutes of presentation and thirty minutes of questions, and the answer was that the hall remains open until 8 p.m. And so it was.

He thanks the audience for their attention and announces that the idea is to continue such gatherings. He conveys that he would gladly come also in the role of a listener and ask questions whenever someone among those present has their own project or a story to tell.

The evening ends with an invitation from the hall for participants not to go home immediately, but to stay for crescent rolls and juices and continue the conversation in an informal atmosphere, in the spirit of the community that the incubator wants to build.
